hints.content: $D$ gives the length of a day in $\blueD{\text{minutes}}$ for a given $\maroonD{\text{day}}$, so $D'$ gives the rate of change of $D$ in $\blueD{\text{minutes}}$ per $\maroonD{\text{day}}$. Specifically, $D'(10)$ is the rate at which the day length changes at $t=10$ days, which is January 10.
In conclusion, this is the best interpretation of $D'(10)=3$:  **On January 10, the day length is increasing at a rate of $3$ minutes per day.**

question.content:
The function $D$ gives the day length, in minutes, of the $n^{\text{th}}$ day of the year in Juneau, Alaska.

**What is the best interpretation for the following statement?**

$D'(10)=3$

[[☃ radio 2]]

choices.content: On January 10, the day length is increasing at a rate of $3$ minutes per day.

choices.clue: This is an interpretation for $D(10)=3$, not for $D'(10)=3$.
choices.content: On January 10, the day is $3$ minutes long.

choices.clue: This is almost correct, but it uses days per minute instead of minutes per day.
choices.content: On January 10, the day length is increasing at a rate of $3$ days per minute.

choices.clue: $D'(10)$ describes the rate of $D$ at a specific point in time, not in an interval of time. This is a wrong interpretation because it talks about an interval of time (until January 10).
choices.content: Until January 10, the day length is increasing at a rate of $3$ minutes per day.
